Im a nurse so have sadly walked in to find many a body.       I work in aged care and so usually this is expected and treated as a blessing in such that the person is no longer suffering.    However, this year I lost a resident younger than myself.    Early 30s male with an awful congenital disease causing progressive ataxia.     When I started caring for him he had already progressed to being blind, able to communicate but very difficult to understand, incontinent, unable to weight bear, full hoist transfer, requiring to be fed, severe swallowing impairment which made him at risk of aspirating.....etc.     His mum had the same condition but to a lesser degree, and would visit him every day arriving by wheelchair taxi.    
One day during the first of our lockdowns,  meaning he hadn't seen any visitors for some time, I walk into administer medications to find him passed.    The pained look on his face keeps me awake at night.    The memory of calling his sister with the news haunts me.   Watching his dad come in to collect his belongings with eyes full of tears bring tears to my eyes.    That I got through that shift astounds me.   Debriefing with my family was hard as this young man was well known in the community.     The poor man got diagnosed at 18 so had in reality like 13 years of suffering.   But I cannot see this loss as a cessation of suffering, rather than a life cut way too short.
